[b]Reading the values[/b]
The current 80 mm orange clownfish has not been species-calibrated. ref_O, ref_ATP and ref_E are independent reference units; they cannot be converted into real oxygen consumption, ATP concentrations or joules. Heart rate is relative, not measured BPM. Health is a stress proxy.

[b]Environment[/b]
WOA23 annual historical boundary: 26.762°C, salinity 35.156, oxygen 204.543 µmol/kg. The baseline 101.886% air saturation is only a fixed scale; warming does not solve oxygen solubility. Solar geometry is an analytical cosine for a reference date, not irradiance. Flow speed, nutrients and local error are unknown.

[b]Full chain and assigned response times[/b]
Water exchange 12 s → Gill uptake 4 s → Circulation proxy 8 s / Heart rate 10 s → Cellular oxygen 12 s → ATP accumulation. Time constants are not total delays or species measurements.
ATP production is constrained by oxygen allocation, a substrate proxy and ADP feedback; consumption rises with cardiac workload. ATP+ADP=20; oxidative flux is limited by the oxygen-supply budget. Only oxidative phosphorylation is modeled. Glycolysis, lactate, pH and other processes are unknown.

[b]All authored reference parameters[/b]
Oxygen threshold 25%, cardiac allocation 4%, ATP/oxygen reference conversion 5, Q10=2; temperature 45 s, producers 120 s, coral 180 s, stress 90 s. Normal oxygen, hypoxia, food, risk, shading and warming are controllable scenarios. Reference cycle 300 s: boundary oxygen declines during 40–100 s, stays at 6% of baseline during 100–190 s, and recovers during 190–260 s.

[b]Display and scientific limitations[/b]
Fish movement, heartbeat and mitochondrial processes read the reference state. Particles and phases are illustrative. Molecule and atom views retain structural explanations; environmental changes do not change atomic structure. The coral proxy is not real bleaching; the reference system does not predict death.
